papers.title: From Sampled Outcomes to Capability Distributions: Rethinking Supervision for LLM Routing
papers.code_version: Mutable main body retrieved. Exact Git commit was not retrieved.

mechanism.observations: Meaning-preserving query rewrites and repeated stochastic decoding
mechanism.paper_targets: Continuous regression targets, hard utility argmax, temperature-softmax utilities, and pairwise/listwise preferences are all described.
mechanism.read_code: Classification uses utility.argmax(axis=2). Softmax mode minimizes the probability-weighted utility regret and does not use the chosen champion as its loss label.
mechanism.exact_tie_scope: The read paper sections do not specify an alternative deterministic hard-label tie convention. The read classification code inherits first-maximum argmax behavior.

papers.data_verification: A scored dataset release is documented by the authors. Raw observations, exact release revision and empirical results were not downloaded or reproduced in this lookup.

papers.title: When LLM Routers Overpay: The Cost of Strong-Model Preference
papers.venue_status: The arXiv author comment reports acceptance to NeurIPS2026. An independent proceedings entry was not checked.

older_version.title: When Routing Collapses: On the Degenerate Convergence of LLM Routers

mechanism.preferences: Meaningfully higher utility takes precedence. Within the specified utility tolerance, lower cost establishes the pairwise preference.
mechanism.loss: CARO is a query-normalized weighted pairwise logistic objective, combined with pointwise utility MSE.
mechanism.label_prior_analysis: AppendixB.6 explicitly discusses winning-label construction, class imbalance and deterministic utility-tie handling as sources of model-specific label priors.
mechanism.permutation_analysis: AppendixB.3 permutes a controlled model-level score component across model identities to test its directional alignment.

papers.code_verification: Repository and README were read. Raw train/method source fetches returned tool cache failures, so executable loss details were checked against the primary v2 full text rather than attributed to uninspected code.
papers.data_verification: No released routing matrix or model weight was downloaded or independently evaluated.

papers.title: Smart Predict, then Optimize

mechanism.consistency_scope: The stated population theorem uses an unrestricted measurable predictor class and sufficient assumptions including conditional continuity and central symmetry. Its stated assumption also lists uniqueness of the mean optimum and nonempty feasible-region interior.
mechanism.discrete_routing_boundary: A binary or three-repeat reward distribution does not satisfy the theorem's continuity condition. Symmetrizing tie handling alone supplies no replacement calibration or generalization theorem.

papers.source_code_status: No original SPO code repository was verified in this targeted lookup.

access_gaps: GitHub commit API URLs were inaccessible through the web tool, so neither repository is commit-pinned here.
EquiRouter raw source endpoints returned cache-miss failures. These failures do not establish that the files or repository are absent.
The NSF-hosted accepted manuscript endpoint returned502. Author-version SPO full text and the INFORMS metadata record were accessible.
This targeted review cannot establish global novelty or reproduce authors' reported numerical improvements.

independent_reasoning.origin: Derived for the E17 claim audit, not quoted as a theorem of the cited papers
independent_reasoning.tie_champion_difference: For r,t both true maximizers, L_t-L_r=2*(s_r-s_t).

permutation_vs_calibration_example.loss: Uniformly average the true-maximizer SPO+ losses; let score vector=(d,0).
permutation_vs_calibration_example.scope: Counterexample to the general implication from tie/permutation symmetry to expected-reward calibration, not an empirical claim about the MAB cache or every possible repair.
